name: Masseter Botox

lead: Masseter Botox is the injection of botulinum toxin type A into the masseter, the main chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw. The goal is to weaken the muscle so it shrinks over time, slimming a square or wide lower face. It is also used for teeth grinding and jaw pain.

Looksmaxxing forums discuss it both as a facial slimming option and as something that suits some skull shapes and not others. Several pharma-sponsored trials of onabotulinumtoxinA for masseter prominence have been registered, while use for appearance has been off-label.

paras: Botulinum toxin blocks the release of acetylcholine at the nerve-muscle junction, which causes the injected muscle to weaken [18]. With less use, the masseter is reported to lose bulk over weeks [2].

Reviews describe adverse effects as minimal and short-lasting [2], while Wikipedia notes that injecting the masseter can reduce chewing ability and that spread of toxin can weaken unintended muscles [18]. Researchers have examined whether reduced chewing load changes jawbone density; one placebo-controlled trial found no clinically significant change [3], while a smaller retrospective radiograph study in bruxism patients found region-specific reductions in a bone texture measure [5].

lead: Masseter Botox is the injection of botulinum toxin type A into the masseter muscle, the thick muscle that closes the jaw [1]. It is used to treat masseter muscle hypertrophy or prominence, a benign enlargement that can widen the lower face, and to treat bruxism (teeth grinding) and jaw pain [2][3]. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to slim the lower face and soften a boxy jaw outline.

Reviews report that botulinum toxin injected into the lower back portion of the masseter decreases muscle bulk and reshapes the lower face, with improvements in clenching symptoms and adverse effects described as minimal and short-lasting [3]. A 2022 review noted that there were no standard guidelines for the procedure [2]. Several company-sponsored randomized trials of onabotulinumtoxinA for masseter prominence have been conducted [4][5][6].

Interest in the procedure is visible in search data: a Google Trends analysis of 20 cosmetic procedures reported that search interest in masseter Botox changed by more than 50 percent within single weeks, one of four terms that did [7].

paras: The masseter has superficial, deep and coronoid heads and elevates the jaw; it can enlarge in people who habitually clench or grind their teeth or chew gum constantly, sometimes unilaterally and causing facial asymmetry [1]. Botulinum toxin acts by cleaving SNAP-25 in nerve terminals so that acetylcholine cannot be released, producing flaccid paralysis until the nerve regenerates its proteins [8].

A 2022 review of 14 studies with at least 10 participants assessed botulinum toxin for lower-face contouring in masseter hypertrophy, looking at units injected, injection points, adverse events and duration [2]. A 2019 review concluded that treatment reduces muscle bulk and reshapes the lower face, and may reduce shear stress on jaw bones [3].
Reviewers describe use for bruxism, with reported improvements in grinding, clenching and pain [3]. A trial compared Botox with an occlusal splint for masseter pain [9].

The 2019 review reported that treatment decreases muscle bulk and improves quality-of-life measures such as pain and clenching [3]. A double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation Phase 2 study of onabotulinumtoxinA in 187 adults with masseter muscle prominence provided the sample for a later imaging analysis [10][11]. Phase 3 programmes starting in 2023 and 2024 enrolled roughly 200 to 260 participants each [5][6].

The 2019 review described adverse effects as minimal and short-lasting [3]. Wikipedia's botulinum toxin article lists unintended muscle weakness from toxin spread, headaches, flu-like symptoms and allergic reactions as reported effects of cosmetic use, and notes that masseter injection can reduce chewing ability [8]. A porcine study examined histological and myosin changes in masticatory muscle after toxin treatment [12].

Researchers have asked whether weaker chewing load could reduce mandibular bone density. In a prespecified subpopulation of 123 people from the 12-month placebo-controlled study, CT scans showed no clinically significant bone density change versus placebo or baseline after one or two treatments [10]. A follow-up CT study of bone morphology has also been published [13]. A retrospective study of 42 bruxism patients receiving 50 units of toxin found statistically significant reductions in a fractal dimension measure in the angulus region, with no significant difference compared with controls after treatment [14].

Published human research includes reviews [2][3], a randomized placebo-controlled CT study [10], and a retrospective radiographic study [14]. Registered trials include Phase 2 and Phase 3 studies of onabotulinumtoxinA for masseter prominence [4][11][5][6] and a Phase 4 comparison with an occlusal splint for masseter pain [9]. A study of Instagram posts tagged masseter Botox rated information reliability in video posts as very low [15], and a review of internet information on Botox for bruxism assessed quality of English resources [16].

On looksmax.org, users post before-and-after results; one reports receiving 10 units per side seeking lower-third slimming and relief from jaw tension, and a reply suggests implants would have been preferable [17]. Another poster reports receiving different amounts on each side to correct asymmetry, describes new hollowing, and cautions that the treatment should be reserved for extreme bruxism [18]. Forum users also debate which skull shapes it suits, which is opinion rather than research finding.

lore.intro: Forum posts treat masseter Botox as a lower-face slimming option with trade-offs for skull shape, asymmetry and bone structure, often compared with implants [17][18].

claims.claim: Masseter Botox slims the lower face and gives hollows.
It should be reserved for bruxism or extreme cases.
The toxin may weaken the jawbone.
